Phenylacetic acid (PAA), molecular formula C8H8O2, was isolated and structurally characterized from the water-soluble fraction of the vaginal symbiont Chryseobacterium gleum cultured at pH 7.3 using NMR and MS.
PAA production by C. gleum was significantly higher when cultured at pH 7.3 (mimicking vaginitis-like conditions) than at pH 5.5, with the difference increasing over 7 days of culture.

RNA-seq revealed that the gene encoding phenylacetyl-CoA epoxidase subunit A (RS19060), along with nearby PaaC/PaaJ homolog genes (RS19070, RS19080), was among the most upregulated genes at pH 7.3 versus pH 5.5, suggesting clustered PAA metabolism genes regulated by pH.
PAA inhibited growth of the bacterial vaginosis pathogen Gardnerella vaginalis with an IC50 of 12.4 mM.
PAA inhibited growth of the vulvovaginal candidiasis pathogen Candida albicans with an IC50 of 18.1 mM.

PAA showed weaker, less potent inhibitory activity against beneficial vaginal Lactobacillus spp. (IC50 26.3-31.3 mM) than against pathogens, and its reduction of L. iners viability was not statistically significant, suggesting selectivity for pathogens.

Intravaginal PAA dose-dependently reduced myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity in Gardnerella vaginalis- and Candida albicans-induced vaginitis in mice, with the 1 mg/mouse dose outperforming clotrimazole 2 mg/mouse and approaching normal levels.
PAA significantly inhibited GV- and CA-stimulated prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) levels in vaginal tissue of mice.
PAA treatment dose-dependently and significantly reduced GV- and CA-induced NF-κB p65 activation and COX-2 expression in vaginal tissue of mice.
PAA at concentrations up to 50 μM for 24 hours had no effect on the viability of human mast cells (HMC-1), indicating its anti-mast-cell effects are not due to cytotoxicity.
PAA decreased compound 48/80-stimulated degranulation (β-hexosaminidase release) in human mast cells (HMC-1) in a concentration-dependent manner, indicating suppression of mast cell activation.
PAA reduced compound 48/80-stimulated LTC4 secretion from human mast cells (HMC-1) in a concentration-dependent manner.
PAA reduced compound 48/80-stimulated PGD2 secretion from human mast cells (HMC-1) in a concentration-dependent manner.

PAA (50 μM) reduced activation of the mast cell signaling molecules PLCγ1, Akt, p38, ERK1/2, and IKK, which are positive regulators of mast cell activation, consistent with its inhibitory effect on degranulation and eicosanoid release.

In a hemodialysis patient, administration of the radiocontrast agent iopamidol triggered Kounis syndrome, an acute coronary syndrome linked to mast cell activation, confirmed by ECG and echocardiographic evidence of cardiac ischemia despite the absence of cutaneous allergic signs.

Intramuscular adrenaline (0.3 mg), given 18 minutes after symptom onset, stabilized the patient's vital signs and improved his ECG, echocardiographic findings, and symptoms of radiocontrast-induced Kounis syndrome.

The authors caution that in hemodialysis patients, radiocontrast media causing Kounis syndrome may not be adequately excreted and could remain injurious, so the decision to perform emergency coronary angiography in radiocontrast-induced Kounis syndrome should be made cautiously with close monitoring instead.
Pooled analysis of BAT stimulated with peanut extract showed a specificity of 96% and sensitivity of 86% for diagnosing peanut allergy.
BAT diagnostic accuracy was lower when stimulated with the Ara h 2 component compared to peanut extract.
BAT was able to discriminate between allergic and merely sensitized peanut patients with a pooled sensitivity of 86% and specificity of 97%.
Only one study provided data on MAT for peanut allergy diagnosis, which precluded statistical meta-analysis, and the authors call for more investigation into MAT as a diagnostic method.

An artificial neural network model built from seven mitochondria-related genes achieved an AUC of 0.984 for scleroderma diagnosis in the training data, 0.980 on cross-validation, and 0.740 on the independent verification dataset GSE76807.

Using random forest, LASSO regression and SVM algorithms on differentially expressed mitochondria-related genes, seven genes (POLB, GSR, KRAS, NT5DC2, NOX4, IGF1, TGM2) were identified as the most relevant biomarkers for scleroderma.
RT-qPCR in a mouse model of scleroderma confirmed significant up-regulation of POLB, GSR, KRAS, NOX4, IGF1 and TGM2 mRNAs.
RT-qPCR in the mouse scleroderma model showed significant down-regulation of NT5DC2 mRNA, contrasting with its bioinformatic classification alongside other up-regulated candidate genes.
CIBERSORT-based immune cell infiltration analysis found that differentially expressed genes in scleroderma were associated with mast cell activation among other immune cell populations.

Beyond mast cells, the differential genes in scleroderma were also associated with altered proportions of follicular helper T cells, immature B cells, resting dendritic cells, memory activated CD4+ T cells, M0 macrophages, monocytes, and resting memory CD4+ T cells.
Genetic deletion of MrgprB2 completely abolished restraint stress-induced periorbital mechanical hypersensitivity in mice.
Restraint stress transiently elevated blood PACAP38 concentrations immediately after stress cessation, returning to baseline by 24 hours, in both wild-type and MrgprB2-deficient mice.
Dura mater PACAP38 levels did not change after restraint stress, suggesting circulating rather than locally-released PACAP38 drives stress-induced headache behaviour.
PACAP38 application increased degranulation of peritoneal mast cells from wild-type mice but not from MrgprB2-deficient mice.
PACAP38 also induced degranulation in the human mast cell line LAD2.
Direct dural injection of PACAP38 induced periorbital mechanical hypersensitivity lasting 24 hours in wild-type mice, which was completely absent in MrgprB2-deficient mice.
PACAP38 dural injection significantly increased grimace pain scores in wild-type mice, lasting 24 hours, an effect abolished in MrgprB2-deficient mice.
Sensory-neuron-specific or blood-vessel-specific conditional knockout of PAC1 did not reduce stress-induced headache behaviour, indicating PAC1 is not required.
Pharmacological inhibition of PAC1 with PA-8 did not block stress-induced headache behaviour.
PAC1 inhibitor PA-8 also had no effect on PACAP38-induced headache behaviour, consistent with a PAC1-independent mechanism.
PACAP38 directly activated HEK293 cells expressing mouse MrgprB2 or its human ortholog MRGPRX2, evoking Ca2+ transients.
PACAP38-induced Ca2+ transients in mast cells were blocked by MrgprB2 genetic deficiency in mouse cells and by the MRGPRX2-specific inhibitor QWF in human LAD2 cells, confirming receptor specificity.
Dural PACAP38 injection significantly increased the number of degranulated mast cells in dura mater in vivo in wild-type but not MrgprB2-deficient mice.
In vivo intact-dura imaging using Mrgprb2-cre:GCaMP6 mice showed that PACAP38 application significantly increased Ca2+ transients in dura mast cells.
PACAP38 application onto dura mater increased Ca2+ transients in trigeminal afferent nerve fibres in vivo.
PACAP38 application significantly increased dura mater blood vessel diameter (vasodilation), an effect dependent on MrgprB2.
Restraint stress increased the number of spontaneously active TG neurons across small, medium, and large diameter classes, and this increase was abolished in MrgprB2-deficient mice.
PACAP38 dural injection selectively increased spontaneous activity in small-diameter TG neurons in wild-type but not MrgprB2-deficient mice, with no change in medium/large neurons.

Restraint stress increased TG neuron activation in response to mechanical (0.4g von Frey) stimulation of the V1 (ophthalmic) region, restricted to small-diameter neurons, with no effect in the V2 region.
Capsaicin injection into the V1 region, but not V2, evoked increased TG neuron activation in stressed mice, consistent with TRPV1-mediated chemical sensitization.

Dural PACAP38 injection increased TG neuron responses to von Frey and capsaicin stimulation in the V1 region (mirroring stress), and this sensitization was completely abolished in MrgprB2-deficient mice.
The TRPV1 inhibitor SB366791 reversed restraint stress-induced periorbital mechanical hypersensitivity when given prior to testing.
The TNF-α receptor inhibitor R-7050, given prior to restraint stress, prevented stress-induced periorbital mechanical hypersensitivity.
SB366791 (TRPV1 inhibitor) prevented PACAP38-induced periorbital mechanical hypersensitivity, indicating TRPV1 acts downstream of PACAP38-MrgprB2 signalling.
R-7050 (TNF-α receptor inhibitor) prevented PACAP38-induced periorbital mechanical hypersensitivity, indicating TNF-α acts downstream of PACAP38-MrgprB2 signalling.
Patients with CASPR2 antibodies frequently report neuropathic pain, with in vitro and in vivo studies supporting pathogenicity of these antibodies.
Patients with LGI1 antibodies frequently report neuropathic pain, with in vitro and in vivo studies supporting pathogenicity of these antibodies.
Antibodies against TS-HDS have been associated with small fiber neuropathy in the reviewed literature.
Antibodies against FGFR3 have been associated with small fiber neuropathy in the reviewed literature.
Antibodies against Plexin-D1 have been associated with small fiber neuropathy in the reviewed literature.
Some studies reported the onset of small fiber neuropathy following COVID-19 infection and vaccination, with investigation of potential autoantibody targets.
Evidence of efficacy of IVIG and plasma exchange in idiopathic SFN supports an underlying autoimmune etiology in some cases.
Whole body insulin sensitivity was positively correlated with the expression of type I (slow-twitch) muscle fibers in healthy young individuals.
Whole body insulin sensitivity was negatively correlated with resting heart rate in healthy young individuals, indicating altered autonomic nervous system function.
Resting heart rate was negatively correlated with type I muscle fiber expression, linking autonomic tone to muscle fiber composition.

Subjects with a high percentage of type I muscle fibers, lower heart rate, and higher insulin sensitivity had higher muscle eNOS protein expression than subjects with low type I fiber percentage, higher heart rate, and lower insulin sensitivity.
eNOS expression was almost twofold higher in pools of type I muscle fibers compared with type II fibers.
eNOS protein was localized exclusively to capillaries surrounding muscle fibers.
Muscle eNOS expression was linearly associated with whole body insulin sensitivity.
An altered function of the autonomic nervous system and compromised microvascular vasodilation capacity occur early in the development of insulin resistance, before clinical disease manifests.
Loeys-Dietz syndrome is an autosomal-dominant connective tissue disorder linked to mutations in the transforming growth factor beta receptor.
A 24-year-old male with developmental delay presented with a one-year history of worsening dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea, ultimately diagnosed with Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

Echocardiography demonstrated right atrial and right ventricular dilation, right ventricular hypertrophy, an atrial septal defect, and aneurysmal dilation of the pulmonary artery trunk in this patient with Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

The authors emphasize the importance of early detection and comprehensive imaging in patients suspected of having Loeys-Dietz syndrome due to potential atypical vascular manifestations such as pulmonary artery dilation and atrial septal defect.
Nearly half of MFS patients showed posterior segment abnormalities, including retinal detachment, maculopathy, and posterior staphyloma.
The location and gene region of FBN1 mutations were significantly associated with incidence of maculopathy.
The location and gene region of FBN1 mutations were significantly associated with the incidence of posterior staphyloma.
Mutations located in the middle region of FBN1 were associated with lower incidence of maculopathy and posterior staphyloma than mutations in the C-terminal region.
Mutations in the TGF-β regulating sequence of FBN1 were associated with a higher incidence of maculopathy and posterior staphyloma.
The location and gene region of FBN1 mutations were also significantly associated with incidence of atrophic maculopathy.
Mutations located in the middle region of FBN1 conferred a significantly lower probability of atrophic maculopathy.
Mutations in the TGF-β regulating region of FBN1 conferred a higher incidence of atrophic maculopathy.
FBN1 mutations located in the TGF-β regulating sequence were associated with a higher incidence of both maculopathy and posterior staphyloma compared to other mutation regions.
The location and region of FBN1 mutations were significantly associated with the incidence of atrophic maculopathy.
FBN1 mutations located in the middle region of the gene were associated with a significantly lower probability of atrophic maculopathy.
FBN1 mutations located in the TGF-β regulating region were associated with a higher incidence of atrophic maculopathy.
GLE treatment reduced skin thickness and lymph node nodule formation in DNCB-induced atopic dermatitis mice.
GLE suppressed the expression and secretion of histamine in mast cells/skin tissue of DNCB-treated mice.
GLE suppressed secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines associated with mast cell-mediated allergic inflammation.
GLE significantly lowered production of inflammatory mediators including ROS, LTC4, PGE2, COX-2, and iNOS in the DNCB-treated mouse model.
GLE inhibited the phosphorylation of MAPK family members ERK, p38, and JNK, which are linked to inflammatory cytokine expression.
GLE inhibited NF-κB activation and blocked the NF-κB and inflammasome pathways underlying its anti-inflammatory effect on mast cell-mediated allergic inflammation.
Ginseng leaf extract's inhibitory effect on mast cell-mediated allergic inflammation was attributed in part to blockade of the inflammasome pathway, in addition to NF-κB inhibition.
Fasting blood glucose was significantly higher in T2DM patients with abnormal gastric electrical rhythm (AGER) compared to those with normal gastric electrical rhythm (NGER).
HbA1c was significantly higher in the AGER group compared to NGER group but was not independently associated with AGER in multivariate analysis.

Low frequency heart rate variability (LF) was significantly reduced in T2DM patients with AGER compared to NGER, reflecting sympathetic autonomic damage, though it was not independently associated with AGER after adjustment.

High frequency heart rate variability (HF) was significantly reduced in T2DM patients with AGER compared to NGER, reflecting vagal autonomic damage, though not independently associated with AGER after adjustment.
The presence of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) was significantly associated with abnormal gastric electrical rhythm (AGER) in univariate analysis but not in multivariate logistic regression.
Diabetic cardiac autonomic neuropathy (DCAN) was significantly associated with abnormal gastric electrical rhythm and remained an independent risk factor in multivariate logistic regression.
T2DM patients as a group showed abnormal gastric slow-wave patterns, with mean pre-meal and postprandial slow-wave ratios below 65% and postprandial bradygastria as the predominant abnormality.
Over half of T2DM patients (50.77%) reported at least one gastrointestinal symptom of gastroparesis, with reduced appetite being the most common symptom and vomiting the least common.

T2DM patients with abnormal gastric electrical rhythm (AGER) had significantly higher prevalence of feeling excessively full after meals, loss of appetite, and visibly larger stomach after meals compared to those with normal gastric electrical rhythm.

Metformin therapy use was not significantly associated with abnormal gastric electrical rhythm status in this cohort, contrasting with prior studies linking metformin to gastrointestinal symptoms in gastroparesis patients.
Tofacitinib reduced the viability and migration capacity of TGF-β1-induced HFL-1 lung fibroblasts.
TGF-β1 induction significantly up-regulated α-SMA gene expression in HFL-1 cells compared with the blank control group.
5.0 μmol/L tofacitinib significantly inhibited TGF-β1-induced α-SMA gene expression compared with the induction group.
Tofacitinib at 0.5-5.0 μmol/L significantly inhibited TGF-β1-induced FN gene expression compared with the induction group.
COL1 gene expression did not change significantly with tofacitinib intervention compared with the TGF-β1-induced group.
FN1 protein levels showed a downward trend with increasing tofacitinib concentration but the reduction compared with the TGF-β1-induced group did not reach statistical significance.

Unlike α-SMA and FN1, COL1A1 protein expression did not significantly differ between the TGF-β1-induced group and control, and tofacitinib intervention produced no further change in COL1A1 protein levels.
TGF-β1 upregulated IL-6 gene expression in HFL-1 cells at 48 hours, and this induction was partly inhibited by tofacitinib intervention.
IL-6 protein levels in culture supernatant were increased by TGF-β1 induction and this increase was partly inhibited by tofacitinib treatment.
Tofacitinib at 5.0 µmol/L significantly inhibited TGF-β1-induced upregulation of α-SMA (ACTA2) gene expression in HFL-1 cells.
Fibronectin (FN) gene expression was significantly inhibited by tofacitinib across all tested concentrations (0.5–5.0 µmol/L) compared with TGF-β1 induction alone.
COL1 gene expression did not change significantly with tofacitinib intervention compared with TGF-β1 induction alone.
α-SMA protein levels decreased with tofacitinib intervention, reaching statistical significance at 2.0 and 5.0 µmol/L compared with TGF-β1 induction alone.
FN1 protein levels showed a downward trend with tofacitinib intervention but did not reach statistical significance compared with TGF-β1 induction alone.
Among 2980 children hospitalized with acute SARS-CoV-2, 18.0% (536) had a severe neurological manifestation during hospitalization.
Among 588 children hospitalized with MIS-C, 24.8% (146) had a severe neurological manifestation during hospitalization.

In surviving children hospitalized with acute SARS-CoV-2, severe neurological manifestations were independently associated with higher odds of new neurocognitive and/or functional morbidity at hospital discharge after adjustment for covariates.

In surviving children hospitalized with MIS-C, severe neurological manifestations were independently associated with higher odds of new neurocognitive and/or functional morbidity at hospital discharge after adjustment for covariates.
In-hospital mortality was markedly higher among children with acute SARS-CoV-2 who had severe neurological manifestations compared with those who did not.
In-hospital mortality was higher among children with MIS-C who had severe neurological manifestations compared with those who did not.
Admission platelet counts were lower in children with severe neurological manifestations than in those without, in both the acute SARS-CoV-2 and MIS-C groups.
C-reactive protein, lymphocyte counts, and sodium levels did not differ significantly between children with and without severe neurological manifestations.
New neurocognitive morbidity alone (PCPC-based) was more common in survivors of acute SARS-CoV-2 with severe neurological manifestations than in those without.
New functional morbidity alone (FSS-based) was more common in survivors of acute SARS-CoV-2 with severe neurological manifestations than in those without.
New neurocognitive morbidity alone was more common in survivors of MIS-C with severe neurological manifestations than in those without.
New functional morbidity alone was more common in survivors of MIS-C with severe neurological manifestations than in those without.
Preexisting neurological comorbidity was more common among children with severe neurological manifestations than those without, in both acute SARS-CoV-2 and MIS-C.
Sympathetic storming or dysautonomia was among the severe neurological manifestations observed in children with MIS-C, occurring in 10.9% of those with severe manifestations.
Acute encephalopathy was the most common severe neurological manifestation in both acute SARS-CoV-2 (61.9%) and MIS-C (76.0%) groups.
Children with severe neurological manifestations (both acute SARS-CoV-2 and MIS-C) underwent neuroimaging and EEG far more frequently than those without.
Children with acute SARS-CoV-2 and severe neurological manifestations were more likely to receive remdesivir, corticosteroids, and IVIG than those without severe neurological manifestations.
In MIS-C, remdesivir use was more frequent among children with severe neurological manifestations, but corticosteroid and IVIG use did not differ by severe neurological manifestation status.

Children with severe neurological manifestations (both acute SARS-CoV-2 and MIS-C) more frequently received inpatient rehabilitation-related services (physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, rehabilitation consults) than those without.
80% of surveyed participants reported experiencing Long COVID with symptoms persisting for over three months.
Individuals with multiple COVID-19 infections showed a significant increase in general symptom scores compared to those with single infection.
Individuals with multiple COVID-19 infections showed a significant increase in cardiovascular symptom scores.
Individuals with multiple COVID-19 infections showed a significant increase in neuropsychological symptom scores.
Individuals with multiple COVID-19 infections reported significantly higher total distress scores due to symptoms.
Participants classified into the 'Mild Symptomatology' latent class showed significantly lower distress due to symptoms compared to other classes.
Participants classified into the 'Severe Symptomatology' latent class showed significantly higher distress due to symptoms compared to other classes.
Latent Class Analysis identified three distinct symptomatology classes among Long COVID patients: 'Diverse', 'Mild', and 'Severe'.
A reduction in the butyrate-producing genus Faecalibacterium (along with Roseburia and Clostridium) has been reported in ME/CFS and proposed as a potential diagnostic biomarker.
ME/CFS patients show higher levels of pro-inflammatory Gram-negative bacteria (Alistipes, Bacteroidetes, Enterobacteriaceae) compared with healthy controls, associated with worse disease course.
Reduced abundance of Actinobacteria has been reported in ME/CFS and is linked to GI conditions (IBD, IBS) and neuropsychiatric disease.

ME/CFS patients with comorbid IBS and high anxiety/depression symptoms had significantly lower alpha diversity of gut microbiome than healthy controls and IBS-only cohorts, with higher Proteobacteria, Prevotellaceae and Bacteroides and lower Lachnospiraceae.
Long COVID patients show reduced commensal species (E. rectale, F. prausnitzii, Bifidobacterium spp.) persisting for up to 30 days, with microbial richness not recovering even after 6 months.

In an observational study, 76% of an initial sample of 106 patients developed long COVID symptoms at 6 months and had higher Ruminococcus gnavus and Bacteroides vulgatus, and lower Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, correlated with persistent respiratory, neuropsychiatric and fatigue symptoms.

A prospective follow-up study of COVID-19 survivors reported significantly reduced bacterial diversity and lower relative abundance of SCFA-producing bacteria a year after discharge, correlating with persistent physical, psychiatric and lung function impairment.
Eight weeks of Lactobacillus casei strain Shirota supplementation significantly reduced inflammatory markers in ME/CFS patients.
Eight weeks of oral Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 decreased CRP and IL-6 compared with baseline in 70% of ME/CFS patients, suggesting systemic (not just mucosal) effects.

Eight weeks of multi-strain probiotic formulations (Ramnoselle, Cytogenex) improved fatigue (Chalder's score), reduced CRP by almost 30%, increased IgM three-fold, and reduced CD4/CD8 ratio in ME/CFS patients.

A 4-week multi-strain probiotic trial improved SF-12 neurocognitive scoring but showed no significant improvement in fatigue or physical activity (VAS) scores, and no major gut microbiota compositional change, in ME/CFS patients.

Three weeks of the multi-strain probiotic SLAB51 (Sivomixx800®) significantly lowered the proportion of long COVID patients reporting fatigue on the FAS scale compared with untreated individuals, with associated metabolic changes.
Four weeks of the 8-strain probiotic VSL#3 significantly reduced Chalder fatigue scale scores in long COVID patients compared with placebo, with effects maintained 4 weeks post-intervention.
Despite improving fatigue, VSL#3 failed to improve performance/somatization symptoms and psychiatric outcomes (anxiety, depression) in a neuropsychiatric sequelae trial after 4 weeks.

A multi-enzyme/probiotic formulation (ImmunoSEB) significantly reduced total physical and mental fatigue scores and CRP levels (77% reduction vs 56% for placebo) in COVID-19 patients, with enhanced recovery by day 10 and no adverse events.

A synbiotic combining probiotic strains, inulin, and a phytochemical blend led to an almost two-fold reduction in mean fatigue scores and doubled improvement in subjective well-being scores after 4 weeks compared with placebo.

In a small study of females co-diagnosed with fibromyalgia and ME/CFS, a synbiotic formulation reduced perceived fatigue, fibromyalgia impact, anxiety, and improved pain and sleep quality versus baseline.

A 6-month pilot study of a 9-strain probiotic formulation with prebiotics and micronutrients improved fatigue, mood and quality of life in both probiotic and placebo groups, with greater improvement in the probiotic group; depression and well-being improved in 44.3% (n=27) of self-assessed long COVID participants.
Twelve weeks of Lactobacillus paracasei HII01 supplementation significantly reduced salivary cortisol levels compared with baseline in fatigued participants.

Seven days of a multi-strain probiotic reduced diarrhea and severity of infection symptoms and was associated with an eight-fold reduced risk of respiratory failure among hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Thirty days of a synbiotic (Lactobacillus strains plus inulin) significantly improved gut health and reduced GI symptoms, especially in older patients with more severe disease, along with improved fatigue, indigestion and cough in long COVID.

A phase 3 clinical trial found VSL#3 effective in ameliorating GI symptoms as measured by SAGIS compared with placebo, but with limited effects on acid regurgitation, nausea, vomiting, constipation, epigastric pain and IBS-like symptoms.
GI symptoms and IBS co-diagnosis are reported as a frequent comorbidity, affecting up to 92% of ME/CFS patients.
An 8-week course of Lactobacillus casei strain Shirota significantly reduced inflammatory markers in ME/CFS patients.
An 8-week course of oral Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 decreased CRP and IL-6 concentrations compared with baseline in 70% of ME/CFS patients, suggesting systemic as well as mucosal effects.

Multi-strain probiotic formulations (Ramnoselle and Cytogenex) taken for 8 weeks ameliorated fatigue in ME/CFS patients, associated with a ~30% reduction in CRP, a three-fold increase in IgM, and a reduced CD4/CD8 ratio, though high inter-patient variability limits conclusions.

A 4-week multi-strain probiotic supplement improved SF-12 neurocognitive functioning scores in ME/CFS patients but showed no significant improvement in fatigue or physical activity scores (VAS) or major gut microbiota changes.

Probiotic interventions in COVID-19 patients using multiple Lactobacillus/Bifidobacterium/Pediococcus/Streptococcus strains lowered systemic inflammation and serum CRP and improved cough and shortness of breath, but had no obvious effect on fever, headache, or weakness.

The commercial probiotic Sivomixx800 (SLAB51) significantly lowered the proportion of long COVID patients reporting fatigue on the FAS scale after 3 weeks compared with untreated individuals, with favorable changes in glucose-metabolism metabolites.

VSL#3 probiotic supplementation for 4 weeks significantly reduced Chalder fatigue scale scores in long COVID patients compared with placebo, with the effect maintained through a 4-week post-intervention period.

A multi-enzyme probiotic formulation (ImmunoSEB) significantly reduced total physical and mental fatigue scores and CRP levels (77% reduction vs 56% with placebo) in COVID-19 patients, was well tolerated with no adverse events, and enhanced recovery by day 10.

A synbiotic combining five probiotic strains with inulin and a phytochemical-rich food blend produced an almost two-fold reduction in mean fatigue scores and doubled subjective well-being scores after 4 weeks compared with placebo.
In a small study of females with comorbid fibromyalgia and ME/CFS, a synbiotic formulation reduced perceived fatigue and fibromyalgia impact compared with baseline.

A multi-component probiotic/prebiotic/micronutrient preparation improved fatigue, mood, and quality of life in both probiotic and placebo groups after 6 months, with greater improvements in the probiotic group.

Clostridium butyricum (CBM588) added to antidepressant treatment significantly reduced HAMD-17 and BDI depression scores (≥50% reduction) in treatment-resistant major depressive disorder patients compared with placebo.
Twelve weeks of Lactobacillus paracasei HII01 supplementation significantly reduced salivary cortisol levels compared with baseline in fatigued participants.

The same multi-strain probiotic formulations improved ME/CFS patients' capability to respond to stress, shown as a 2.4-fold increase in urinary free cortisol and a 1.4-fold increase in DHEA-S, alongside improved BDI mood scores.

Despite reducing fatigue, a 28-day VSL#3 intervention failed to improve somatization symptoms or psychiatric outcomes (anxiety, depression) in long COVID patients, suggesting limited effectiveness in modulating the gut-brain axis for psychiatric symptoms.
A prebiotic FOS plus multi-strain probiotic mixture significantly decreased depressive symptoms in moderately depressed patients compared with placebo.
Over 6 months, OMNi-BiOTiC STRESS Repair 9 improved symptoms of depression and perceived emotional well-being in 44.3% (n=27) of self-assessed long COVID participants.
After 4 weeks, the Gasteel Plus synbiotic significantly reduced anxiety compared with baseline in women with fibromyalgia and ME/CFS, along with improvements in pain perception and sleep quality.

A 7-day multi-strain probiotic regimen reduced diarrhea and infection-related symptom severity and was associated with an eight-fold reduced risk of respiratory failure among hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

A 30-day synbiotic intervention with Lactobacillus strains and inulin led to significant improvements in gut health and reduced GI symptoms, and also improved fatigue, indigestion and cough, especially in older patients with more severe long COVID.
After 3 months, OMNi-BiOTiC STRESS Repair 9 led to subjective improvement in GI health including enhanced digestion and reduced diarrhea, constipation, flatulence, and abdominal pain.

In a phase 3 clinical trial, VSL#3 was effective in ameliorating overall GI symptoms measured by SAGIS compared with placebo, but had limited effects on acid regurgitation, nausea, vomiting, constipation, epigastric pain, and IBS-like symptoms.

Butyrate supplementation, compared with other short-chain fatty acids acetate and propionate, is proposed as most advantageous due to immunomodulatory effects including increased mucin/defensin secretion, antiviral defense induction (interferon-gamma, granzyme B), and reduced systemic inflammation.

In a pilot study, 6 months of supplementation with a multi-strain probiotic/prebiotic formulation (OMNi-BiOTiC STRESS Repair 9) improved symptoms of depression and perceived emotional well-being in 44.3% of self-assessed long COVID participants.

In women with comorbid fibromyalgia and ME/CFS, 4 weeks of Gasteel Plus synbiotic supplementation significantly reduced anxiety compared with baseline, with additional improvements in pain perception and sleep quality.

Probiotic supplementation with Lactobacilli/Bifidobacteria strains reduced pro-inflammatory mediators CRP, TNF-α and IL-6 in ME/CFS patients, which may help reduce comorbid IBS-like symptoms and improve quality of life.

In females with comorbid fibromyalgia and ME/CFS, Gasteel Plus synbiotic supplementation improved GI health index scores compared with baseline, but the improvement did not reach statistical significance.
Approximately 22% of individuals diagnosed with COVID-19 may experience GI distress, most commonly loss of appetite, dyspepsia, IBS-like symptoms and abdominal pain.

A 7-day multi-strain probiotic preparation reduced diarrhea and other infection symptoms and was associated with an eight-fold reduced risk of respiratory failure among hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

A 30-day synbiotic intervention combining Lactobacillus strains with prebiotic inulin significantly improved gut health and reduced GI symptoms, along with improved fatigue, indigestion and cough, especially in older patients with more severe long COVID.

After 3 months, OMNi-BiOTiC STRESS Repair 9 multi-strain probiotic/prebiotic supplementation led to subjective improvement in GI health, including enhanced digestion and reduced diarrhea, constipation, flatulence and abdominal pain in long COVID patients.

A phase 3 trial of the VSL#3 probiotic formulation significantly improved overall GI symptom scores (SAGIS) versus placebo, but had limited effect on acid regurgitation, nausea, vomiting, constipation, epigastric pain and IBS-like symptoms specifically.

Short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate and butyrate) have immunomodulatory properties proposed to reduce COVID-19 symptom severity, an effect suggested to extend to ME/CFS via gut-brain axis modulation and intestinal barrier strengthening.

Butyrate is proposed to be the most advantageous SCFA due to immunomodulatory effects including increased mucin and defensin secretion, induction of interferon-gamma and granzyme B expression, and reduced systemic inflammation, potentially reducing psychiatric and fatigue symptoms.

Supplementation with live butyrate-producing strains such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Butyricicoccus pullicaecorum is proposed to restore gut homeostasis after inflammation and strengthen the intestinal barrier, potentially preventing leaky gut and associated IBS-like symptoms.
The authors conclude that prebiotic interventions are most likely to alter gut microbiome composition, followed by dietary interventions, and then probiotic interventions, in ME/CFS and long COVID.
TNF-857 TT and CT genotypes were found at increased frequency in ME/CFS patients compared with controls.
A significant decrease in IFN-gamma low producer (A/A) genotype was found in ME/CFS patients compared to controls.
NR3C1-1F DNA methylation was found reduced in ME/CFS patients, consistent with an HPA axis hypofunction hypothesis.
Common mutations in IDO2 (R248W and Y359STOP) are implicated in ME/CFS, suggesting involvement of the kynurenine metabolic pathway.
The ADRB2 (B2AdR) Gln27 polymorphism has been associated with adolescent ME/CFS and, along with Arg16 in adults, may produce an unfavourable cardiovascular profile.
A U.S. health insurance database analysis reported a high narrow-sense heritability estimate (h2=0.48) for ME/CFS.
